title: Root-Selecting Fixed-Point Inversion for Rectified Flows via Trajectory Straightness
claim: Iterative solvers can land on many near-equivalent solutions with different global errors; choosing by a trajectory-level criterion picks the best one.
layout: 2 panels, left-to-right, zoom-in callout with dotted connector lines and a legend
description: The left panel shows three cat photos stacked vertically, with colored trajectories beside them. Green arrows with circle markers trace the inversion path. Orange arrows with diamond markers trace reconstruction paths. Pink arrows mark one-step reconstructions. A dotted ellipse circles several candidate fixed points on the inversion path, and a caption says multiple fixed points with similar residuals but different global errors exist. Dotted lines from the ellipse open into a zoomed panel on the right. That panel is a blue contour landscape, where darker blue means a straighter trajectory. It holds three gray fixed points and one red selected point labeled x_j star. Dashed arrows point from a caption toward these points, and a solid arrow points to the red one. The caption says SelFix selects the fixed point that induces the straightest trajectory. A legend sits at the bottom right. The eye goes first to the red point in the blue landscape.
caption: Overview of SelFix. Fixed-point inversion may produce multiple approximate fixed points with similar residuals but different global reconstruction errors. SelFix uses a causal straightness selector to guide fixed-point iteration toward straighter inverse trajectories, empirically improving reconstruction.
abstract: Finding the initial noise that generates a given data sample, known as inversion, is a key component for downstream applications such as training-free image editing. Existing fixed-point inversion methods improve inversion accuracy by formulating each inversion step as a fixed-point problem, but they lack a principled mechanism for selecting among multiple fixed-point solutions that can arise in practice. We observe that different selections induce different inversion trajectories, leading to substantial variation in reconstruction and editing quality. For rectified flows, we further find that this variation is closely associated with trajectory straightness, motivating straightness as a principled selection criterion. We propose SelFix, a fixed-point inversion method that selects fixed-point solutions inducing straighter inverse trajectories while retaining convergence to an exact inverse root under standard local assumptions. Experiments on FLUX.1-dev and PIE-Bench show that SelFix improves fixed-point inversion, achieving stronger real-image reconstruction and better source-preserving prompt-based editing than prior inversion baselines. The code is available at https://github.com/seminkim/selfix .
